comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C18-C20 regarding FLWR-1 sequence conservation and structural predictions. Both evaluations find these foundational claims well-supported without concerns.
Perfect agreement on claims C3-C9 regarding baseline phenotypic characterization and regulatory role inference. Both evaluations accept these foundational observations as convincing evidence.

Agreement on claims C11-C12 regarding swimming recovery phenotype and rescue. OpenEval evaluates C10-C12 as supported; peer review accepts C11-C12 without challenge, treating this as a valid core phenotype.

Partial disagreement on aldicarb assay interpretation. OpenEval finds claims C13-C17 well-supported with clear statistical evidence. Peer review questions interpretability of aldicarb results (C15-C16, C52, C54, C57-C62), noting they 'may not fully align with direct assessment of neurotransmitter release' and requesting acknowledgment of limitations.

Agreement on localization data (C21-C28). OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence from fluorescence microscopy and RNAseq. Peer review accepts localization studies without challenge, including expression patterns (C29, C31-C32, C34-C35) as part of convincing evidence.

Agreement on active transport evidence (C29-C35). OpenEval finds strong support from moving particles and genetic disruption. Peer review accepts these localization and transport data without challenge.

Disagreement on cell-autonomous interpretation. OpenEval finds claims C36-C46 supported with acknowledgment of complexity. Peer review explicitly challenges cell-autonomy claims (C38-C42), noting combined muscle/cholinergic rescue shows 'non-cell-autonomous interaction' rather than simple autonomy.

Partial overlap on GABAergic function. OpenEval finds C47-C56 well-supported including GABAergic-specific rescue (C52) and GABA release inference (C54). Peer review questions aldicarb-based interpretations of neurotransmitter release, requesting acknowledgment of limitations.

Partial disagreement on genetic epistasis interpretation. OpenEval finds C57-C62 provide strong evidence through elegant genetic dissection. Peer review questions overall interpretability of aldicarb assays for these claims, though accepts the data itself.

Disagreement on Ca2+ imaging interpretation. OpenEval finds C63-C67 provide direct functional evidence for increased Ca2+ and GABA release. Peer review challenges terminology and interpretation, noting lack of direct evidence for 'Ca2+ influx' and possibility of intracellular store mobilization; authors revised to 'Ca2+ elevation.'

Disagreement on Ca2+ phenotype interpretation. OpenEval finds C68-C73 well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer review questions 'Ca2+ influx' terminology and interpretation of 'local' effects; authors withdrew some conclusions and revised terminology.
Agreement on coelomocyte endocytosis data (C74-C78). Both evaluations accept this as valid evidence for conserved endocytic function, consistent with previous work on Flower homologues.

Agreement on pOpsicle assay results (C79-C82, C87, C94). Both evaluations accept the SV recycling kinetics data showing increased fusion signal and slower decay as convincing evidence for defective recycling.

Agreement on electrophysiology data (C85-C86, C88-C91, C93). Both evaluations accept these results as valid evidence. Peer review treats electrophysiology as more direct evidence than aldicarb assays, supporting OpenEval's assessment with acknowledged limitations.

Agreement on TEM ultrastructural data (C96-C97, C99, C101-C102). Both evaluations accept the evidence for reduced SVs and increased endocytic structures. Peer review specifically notes ultrastructural analysis as part of convincing evidence.

Agreement on FLWR-1/MCA-3 genetic interaction (C104-C117). OpenEval finds convergent evidence from multiple assays. Peer review initially requested statistical clarifications for Ca2+ data (C112-C117), which authors provided, then accepted the genetic interaction as supporting a common pathway.

Agreement on E74Q mutant analysis (C118-C123, C132). OpenEval notes partial rescue indicates importance but not essentiality. Peer review accepts these structure-function studies as supporting evidence against Ca2+ channel model.

Agreement on PI(4,5)P2 binding evidence (C124-C131, C133). OpenEval finds convergent computational and experimental evidence compelling. Peer review accepts these results as supporting the proposed mechanism through PI(4,5)P2 rather than Ca2+ channel activity.

Agreement on PI(4,5)P2 reporter data (C135-C142). Both evaluations accept the reduced reporter signal and differential rescue by wild-type vs. mutant FLWR-1 as strong evidence supporting PI(4,5)P2 binding mechanism.

Agreement on BiFC interaction data (C143-C156). OpenEval notes BiFC can produce false positives and need for biochemical confirmation. Peer review accepts BiFC results as supporting evidence while authors acknowledge need for biochemical confirmation.

Perfect agreement on MCA-3 localization effects (C157-C160). Both evaluations accept that FLWR-1 affects MCA-3 distribution, with quantification showing reduced synaptic/axonal ratio supporting the proposed regulatory mechanism.

OpenEval provides summary evaluation of major findings (C161-C168, C228-C230) including conservation of SV recycling function and novel increased neurotransmission finding. No corresponding peer review result explicitly evaluates these summary claims.

OpenEval rates reconciliation with Drosophila studies (C195-C202, C231) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature. No corresponding peer review result explicitly evaluates these comparative discussion claims.

Agreement on rejection of Ca2+ channel hypothesis (C203-C208). OpenEval finds structural and kinetic arguments compelling against Ca2+ channel model. Peer review accepts this conclusion, with editor noting the work 'challenges some previous thinking about FLWR-1 function.'
